english: Let $P$ be the point of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{20}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{5}=1$ with eccentric angle $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, and let $S$ and $S'$ be the foci of the ellipse. Let $U$ and $V$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $S$ and $S'$, respectively, to the tangent to the ellipse at $P$. Let $O$ be the origin. Then the value of $\overrightarrow{OU}\cdot\overrightarrow{OV}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि दीर्घवृत्त $\dfrac{x^{2}}{20}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{5}=1$ का वह बिन्दु $P$ है जिसका उत्केन्द्र कोण $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ है, तथा $S$ और $S'$ दीर्घवृत्त की नाभियाँ हैं। माना $P$ पर दीर्घवृत्त की स्पर्श रेखा पर $S$ तथा $S'$ से डाले गए लम्बों के पाद क्रमशः $U$ तथा $V$ हैं। माना $O$ मूलबिन्दु है। तब $\overrightarrow{OU}\cdot\overrightarrow{OV}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Feet of perpendiculars from the foci to any tangent lie on the auxiliary circle: $OU=OV=a=2\sqrt5$, and $U,V$ are the two points where the tangent meets $x^{2}+y^{2}=20$
Distance of $O$ from the tangent: $p=\dfrac{2\sqrt{10}}{\sqrt5}=2\sqrt2$; half-chord $\sqrt{a^{2}-p^{2}}=\sqrt{12}$
solution_full: Tangent at the point with eccentric angle $\theta$: $\dfrac{x\cos\theta}{a}+\dfrac{y\sin\theta}{b}=1$; for $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$: $\dfrac{x}{2\sqrt{10}}+\dfrac{y}{\sqrt{10}}=1$, i.e. $x+2y=2\sqrt{10}$.

Property: the foot of the perpendicular from a focus to any tangent lies on the auxiliary circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=a^{2}$. So $U$ and $V$ lie on $x^{2}+y^{2}=20$ and on the tangent. They are distinct (the feet from $S$ and $S'$ coincide only if the tangent is perpendicular to the major axis), so they are exactly the two intersection points of the tangent with the circle.
Distance of $O$ from the tangent: $p=\dfrac{2\sqrt{10}}{\sqrt{1+4}}=2\sqrt2$. Half the chord $UV$ is $\sqrt{a^{2}-p^{2}}=\sqrt{20-8}=2\sqrt3$, so $UV^{2}=48$.

Direct check: the foot from $S(\sqrt{15},0)$ on $x+2y=2\sqrt{10}$ is $S-\dfrac{\sqrt{15}-2\sqrt{10}}{5}(1,2)$, and $|OU|^{2}=20$; similarly for $V$, and the dot product computed from the coordinates is $-4$.
originality_note: New: the dot product of the position vectors of the feet of the focal perpendiculars, which the auxiliary-circle property turns into a chord-of-a-circle computation (way 4, hidden symmetry). Closest known: the locus of the feet of perpendiculars from the foci to a tangent is the auxiliary circle; the product of the focal perpendiculars is b^2. Different because: the property is used to replace two foot computations by one chord of the circle, and the quantity asked is a dot product.

Checked that U and V are distinct and are the two intersections of the tangent with the auxiliary circle, and computed the dot product directly from the feet with sympy. Changed: No change.
key_step: Feet of focal perpendiculars lie on x^2 + y^2 = 20, so OU.OV = (OU^2 + OV^2 - UV^2)/2 with UV from the distance 2 sqrt2.
justification: Routine once the auxiliary-circle property is recalled: tangent from the eccentric angle, distance from the centre, chord length, dot product. Comparable to 2021-P2-Q18 (L2), a short ellipse computation with a standard property.

concept_use.Miscellaneous properties of Ellipse: The feet of the perpendiculars from the foci to a tangent lie on the auxiliary circle, so OU = OV = a and U, V are the intersections of the tangent with x^2 + y^2 = 20.
concept_use.Parametric coordinates for Ellipse: P is given by its eccentric angle pi/4, so the tangent at P is x cos theta / a + y sin theta / b = 1, i.e. x + 2y = 2 sqrt 10.
